title: Inventory and capability gates
question: What exact machine and reachable feature set do these experiments target?
setup: Run the supplied read-only Driver API probe plus UUID/BDF, topology, PCIe, NUMA and link-state inspection. Save raw outputs before allocating benchmark buffers.
sweep: Every device and ordered pair; compiler and driver versions separately; idle and steady-load telemetry.
observe: A capability matrix that distinguishes physical identity, peer access, native atomics, VMM, managed memory and stream operations.
baseline: No performance baseline; compare reported inventory to assumptions in a candidate design.
confounders: Device ordinals can change. A supported flag is not an achieved-performance measurement. Do not reset, enable peers or change clocks as part of inventory.
gate: Public read-only queries; errors must be retained, not treated as false or zero.

title: Algebra and encoding checks
question: Are the proposed word circuits and layout equations actually equivalent?
setup: Run tools/semantic_checks.py. Extend with exhaustive small truth tables and deterministic randomized references for any new composition.
sweep: Partial groups, widths, boundary symbols, overflow guards and all small finite states.
observe: Exact agreement for Boolean/routing identities and deliberate failure of insufficient-guard negative controls.
baseline: Simple integer/list reference implementations.
confounders: CPU success does not test GPU rounding, collective participation, compiler lowering or memory ordering.
gate: CPU only; the supplied suite is actually run and logged in this package.

title: Instruction latency versus throughput
question: Which dependency and resource limits govern an exact sm70 instruction form?
setup: Create one true dependent chain and a separate multi-accumulator kernel. Consume results; inspect native SASS and subtract bounded measurement/loop overhead.
sweep: Chain length, independent chains, warps, unrolling, operand forms and register pressure.
observe: A serial latency estimate distinct from independent service throughput and saturation.
baseline: Equivalent scalar operation and empty/loop controls.
confounders: Compiler folding, clock changes, instruction-cache effects and added spills can masquerade as instruction latency.
gate: Public CUDA/PTX initially; B-level variants only after binary validation.

title: Cross-pipeline interference
question: Can two useful operation families overlap without saturating another shared resource?
setup: Time each family alone, serially combined and interleaved at equal semantic work. Preserve enough independent operands to expose overlap.
sweep: INT/FP/tensor/conversion/load mixes; relative work ratios; live-register budget.
observe: Combined critical time closer to a maximum than a sum only where genuine overlap exists; counters explain new bottlenecks.
baseline: Best isolated and serial schedules, not an intentionally poor ordering.
confounders: Shared issue, register ports, HBM and power; extra work invalidates the comparison.
gate: Public/PTX forms; no unsupported later-architecture instructions.

title: Register bank and operand-reuse effects
question: Does operand delivery limit this hot sequence?
setup: Compare semantically identical schedules with controlled operand assignment/reuse. Preserve original cubin and exact transformation.
sweep: Register parity, source reuse, inserted amortized copies and independent instruction spacing.
observe: Repeatable changes tied to distinct bank reads rather than occupancy or arithmetic changes.
baseline: Original compiler output and a dependency-matched schedule.
confounders: Changed live ranges, spills, resource metadata and clock state. Source names do not identify physical registers.
gate: B-level edits require validated tools and complete dependency/resource preservation.

title: Warp routing, matching and lookup
question: When do register exchange and equality grouping beat memory-based structures?
setup: Implement shuffle tables, match-group reservations and mask rank/select with explicit participation. Validate every small index/group shape first.
sweep: Table size, query uniformity, key cardinality, active masks, payload width and reuse.
observe: Break-even surfaces for register/shared/constant lookup and grouped atomics.
baseline: Cached global/shared tables and one-atomic-per-lane plus established aggregation.
confounders: Inactive source lanes, undefined selected values, multiword selection and hidden spills.
gate: Use valid synchronized primitives; do not use incidental activemask as logical membership.

title: Shared banks and phase pipelines
question: Which layout and synchronization phase actually reduces complete movement cost?
setup: Construct controlled broadcast/conflict patterns and producer-consumer tile stages. Keep the semantic data permutation fixed.
sweep: Stride, swizzle, padding, payload width, barrier placement and shared carveout.
observe: Producer-to-consumer timing and conflict behavior, not only a fast standalone store.
baseline: Shuffles for small exchanges and conventional shared tiling.
confounders: Same word broadcast differs from distinct words in one bank. All required participants must reach barriers.
gate: Public shared-memory/barrier contracts; no later mbarrier assumptions.

title: Cache and transaction accounting
question: What fraction of traffic carries useful information, under which reuse conditions?
setup: Use both independent streaming accesses and dependent pointer chains. Separate read/write, warm/cold and cache forms.
sweep: Working set, stride, alignment, active lanes, concurrency and metadata/payload separation.
observe: Latency/throughput/sector signatures consistent with a stated cache or transaction explanation.
baseline: Contiguous useful-byte loads and a deliberately scattered control.
confounders: TLBs, page allocation, compiler elimination and profiler cache flushing. A plateau alone does not prove a cache level.
gate: Public/PTX memory operations with legal cache semantics.

title: Translation working sets and pages
question: Is the irregular workload limited by translation rather than data bandwidth?
setup: Hold useful bytes constant while changing page footprint and traversal order. Record VMM allocation settings separately from observed translation behavior.
sweep: Page count, stride, allocation method, reuse and concurrent requests.
observe: Performance changes with translation footprint that remain after data-cache controls.
baseline: Page-local traversal and conventional contiguous allocation.
confounders: VMM granularity is not automatically TLB page size; VA patterns do not directly reveal physical channel bits.
gate: Only supported allocation/advice/VMM interfaces; no direct PTE modification.

title: MMA lane and register ownership
question: Does the explicit sm70 fragment mapping match the compiled instruction?
setup: Use one-hot/basis inputs and uniquely labeled accumulators. Store raw per-lane outputs before any canonicalizing wrapper.
sweep: Each lane, fragment element, group, row/column form and accumulator type separately.
observe: Full coordinate coverage and exact expected ownership for the tested explicit PTX form.
baseline: CPU coordinate map and scalar small matrix multiplication.
confounders: Opaque WMMA layouts are not the explicit PTX contract; all required lanes execute the instruction.
gate: Compile supported sm70 forms and inspect SASS before interpreting output.

title: Tensor numerical fingerprint
question: Which target-specific rounding and range properties matter to an encoding?
setup: Use targeted exponent gaps, cancellation, ties, subnormals, zeros, large bounded counts and high/low expansions; retain exact references where possible.
sweep: Operand placement, sign, accumulator magnitude, contraction length and conversion order.
observe: A numerical feature table, not only mean error on random matrices.
baseline: Exact integer/rational reference plus explicitly specified scalar floating evaluation orders.
confounders: Input conversion can dominate; equality on easy nonnegative cases does not prove arbitrary FMA equivalence.
gate: No claim of exact tensor counting or certified filtering before this gate and a bound.

title: Tensor versus bitset intersections
question: When do many shared overlap queries repay numeric expansion?
setup: Compute identical intersection counts or threshold decisions with packed AND+POPC, DP4A and supported tensor tiles.
sweep: Universe length, query count, reuse, density, tile padding and requested output sparsity.
observe: Whole-operation crossover including encode/decode and numerical validation.
baseline: Strong packed-bitset implementation with cached cardinalities.
confounders: Computing a dense answer matrix that the application does not need is not equal useful work.
gate: Counts must pass E10 within a proved or conservatively validated bounded domain.

title: Tensor circuits versus structured SIMT
question: Does a small transform benefit from MMA once routing is included?
setup: Compare prefix, reduction, Hadamard/stencil or butterfly components with direct shuffle/add circuits and tensor implementations.
sweep: Number of simultaneous transforms, coefficient reuse, fragment-resident input/output and precision.
observe: The regime where native fragments and reuse beat fewer structured SIMT operations.
baseline: Hand-structured shuffle/add implementation and suitable library path.
confounders: Floating summation order, zero padding, normalization and extraction must be equivalent or bounded.
gate: Use verified fragment mapping and supported sm70 formats.

title: Representation crossover
question: How many uses repay bitplanes, packing or a changed numerical domain?
setup: Implement encoding, steady-state operators and decoding as separately timed stages plus a complete path.
sweep: Reuse count, state cardinality, update rate, partial groups and data distribution.
observe: A measured break-even model that predicts held-out cases.
baseline: Best direct representation including existing packed or vectorized alternatives.
confounders: Omitting maintenance or final decoding creates fictional wins; scalar versus packed output contracts differ.
gate: Run CPU identity checks first; inspect sm70 lowering for packed intrinsics.

title: Atomics as useful coordination
question: How much semantic progress occurs per atomic transaction?
setup: Benchmark reservation, merge and transition workloads with configurable target sharing and optional local aggregation.
sweep: Contention, operation, width, returned-value dependence, distribution and failed CAS fraction.
observe: Useful completed updates/second and latency tails, not merely raw issued attempts.
baseline: Locally aggregated or phased alternatives at equal semantics.
confounders: atomicity does not publish other data. Hot lines and fairness can dominate.
gate: Supported operation and scope on the actual allocation; no race-based shortcut.

title: Publication and progress litmus
question: Can the proposed bounded protocol violate payload or scheduling invariants?
setup: First write a memory-model/progress proof. Then run finite epoch-tagged producer/consumer tests with protected termination and adversarial delays.
sweep: Grid admission, stream ordering, queue fullness, counter wrap bounds and device/host placement.
observe: Any stale payload, reused slot or blocked producer f als if i es the implementation; no observed failures do not prove legality.
baseline: A supported explicit phase/event protocol.
confounders: Undefined races cannot be legalized by stress testing. A watchdog cannot substitute for a schedulable stop path.
gate: No unbounded spin test; use valid memory types, scopes and ordering.

title: Persistent roles and residency
question: When does retained state repay queueing and reserved resources?
setup: Compare bounded resident executors, batched kernels and graphs with the same task stream. Make producer progress explicit.
sweep: Task size, skew, role split, register/shared footprint, occupancy and stop/drain behavior.
observe: End-to-end throughput/tails and state-reuse benefit without starvation.
baseline: Properly batched and graph-replayed conventional execution.
confounders: Assuming all blocks are concurrently resident or treating smid as launch affinity invalidates the design.
gate: Supported cooperative admission where used; otherwise no global spin barrier.

title: DMA and compute overlap
question: Which actors and routes make progress concurrently on this machine?
setup: Time each copy path and compute workload alone, serially and concurrently with explicit legal buffer lifetimes.
sweep: Size, direction, buffer depth, local/peer/host routes and compute memory intensity.
observe: A contention/overlap matrix including owner HBM and critical-path effects.
baseline: SM copy/transform and public asynchronous copy paths.
confounders: Asynchronous return is not physical overlap; roots, copy-engine assignment and power may be shared.
gate: No reset or clock changes; pinned allocation and actual engine capabilities recorded.

title: Peer loads, cache behavior and latency
question: What actually services repeated peer accesses on the tested path?
setup: Use pointer chains and independent requests to peer allocations; compare read-only phases and correctly synchronized writes.
sweep: Working set, stride, cache form, concurrency, allocation and owner-side traffic.
observe: Signatures that separate startup, translation, caching and owner-memory contention.
baseline: Local HBM and explicit peer staging.
confounders: A latency reduction does not by itself prove requester L2 caching or coherent writable aliases.
gate: Validate peer capability and use legal ordering; no unsynchronized cache-coherence tests.

title: Peer signaling and clock relationships
question: How much does a complete GPU-to-GPU handshake cost?
setup: Use a finite epoch protocol with local send/receive intervals and separately estimate clock offset/drift through exchanges.
sweep: Atomic versus event/command paths, polling cadence, message batch size and owner load.
observe: Round-trip and tail latency plus explicit uncertainty for clock alignment.
baseline: CUDA-visible event and staged communication protocols.
confounders: Do not subtract raw timestamps from unsynchronized GPUs. Polling consumes fabric/cache service.
gate: Native peer operation support and a valid publication/progress proof.

title: Actual NVLink routing and saturation
question: Which links carry the traffic, and where does it saturate?
setup: Inventory link connectivity and run directed pair transfers with available link/PCIe telemetry.
sweep: One-way, two-way, multiple streams, all pair combinations and concurrent owner compute.
observe: Measured directional bandwidth and interference tied to the actual topology.
baseline: Each isolated direct pair and supported alternative staging path.
confounders: Bidirectional aggregates cannot be compared with one-way payload rates; counters may include protocol traffic.
gate: No assumed multi-hop forwarding or six-links-per-pair topology.

title: Host NUMA ingress
question: Can locality remove cross-socket traffic or supply independent host paths?
setup: Place and verify host pages on each NUMA node, register/pin them, then transfer to each GPU with controlled producer affinity.
sweep: Local/remote pages, individual/simultaneous directions and mapped versus staged access.
observe: Latency/bandwidth differences explained by page placement and root topology.
baseline: Conventional pinned transfers with verified local placement.
confounders: Pinning and thread affinity do not prove page locality; existing data may originate remotely.
gate: Read-only topology inspection and supported OS allocation/registration.

title: Stream memory operations
question: Which wait/write semantics are reachable and useful on the installed stack?
setup: Query capabilities; test finite value handshakes with explicit CUDA-visible ordering and non-managed supported memory.
sweep: 32/64-bit width, comparison mode, batch size, remote flush support and wrap bounds.
observe: Correct completion and measured full pipeline cost versus shader/event alternatives.
baseline: Events and a tiny bounded polling/update kernel.
confounders: Memory dependencies can be invisible to CUDA scheduling. GEQ wrap semantics are not ordinary unbounded integer comparison.
gate: S17/S42 restrictions must be satisfied before submission.

title: VMM alias and view behavior
question: Can a legal view remove address work without hidden coherence or translation cost?
setup: Query granularity and permissions; construct isolated views with synchronized phase changes and a verified reference.
sweep: View size, alias count, page footprint, window length and access phase.
observe: Correct output plus mapping amortization and translation cost.
baseline: Two-segment ring windows and simple modulo.
confounders: Mapping success is not a complete concurrent-alias visibility contract. Do not remap live accesses.
gate: Public VMM supported by actual device/driver; no PTE edits.

title: Fault and access-counter policy
question: Is coarse remote-access feedback useful before the phase ends?
setup: Observe supported managed-memory advice/prefetch/migration behavior and available notifications under controlled locality phases.
sweep: Phase duration, reuse, working set, advice and owner placement.
observe: Policy lag, migration traffic and total time, not just fault counts.
baseline: Explicit placement and fixed managed policies.
confounders: Notifications may be driver-owned; shared-source defaults are not fixed hardware configuration. Avoid intentional overflow.
gate: No direct ATS/PTE changes without a separately established platform/driver contract.

title: Feedback cost and regret
question: Does adaptation outperform a fixed policy after paying for observation and switching?
setup: Use a small set of already-correct kernels and repeat workloads with known phase changes. Log policy decisions.
sweep: Observation frequency, hysteresis, noise, remaining horizon and switch/repacking cost.
observe: Total regret versus best fixed and offline phase-aware controls.
baseline: Fixed policies and a cheap density/time heuristic.
confounders: profiler replay and thermal drift can change the workload being controlled.
gate: Only installed compatible observation APIs; keep an uninstrumented control.

title: Texture and SFU approximation
question: Can a specialized arithmetic path meet a useful error/performance contract?
setup: Compare table/interpolation, SFU seed/refinement and polynomial implementations over a bounded domain.
sweep: Table spacing, formats, coordinate boundaries, derivative extremes and exceptional values.
observe: Worst-case error and complete execution cost at equal accepted tolerance.
baseline: Conventional function implementation and cached table/manual interpolation.
confounders: Ideal interpolation error omits hardware coordinate/filter/sample precision. Random tests miss extrema.
gate: Documented Tesla CUDA texture/SFU path only; no assumed inaccessible graphics engine.

title: Copy remap reachability
question: Can the declared component transformer be safely invoked and outperform SM formatting?
setup: Before any command, establish an owned driver/channel implementation and exact descriptor rules. Begin with tiny fixed records and a CPU reference.
sweep: expressible component selections, constants, widths, pitches and transfer sizes.
observe: Correct transformation and full cost versus public copy plus/fused shader transform.
baseline: Public memcpy and optimized SM conversion.
confounders: Header fields do not provide complete ownership/format/lifetime semantics. No arbitrary gather assumed.
gate: K-level, NOT executable from the package; requires separate privileged engineering and recovery plan.

title: Copy-engine semaphore actor
question: Can completion-word operations replace a shader boundary in a real pipeline?
setup: Establish a valid command route from pinned HAL evidence. Test release, increment and timestamp separately on isolated owned control storage.
sweep: Counter values, INC/DEC threshold/wrap rules, flush modes and command sequencing.
observe: Exact word semantics and complete pipeline latency without payload transfer.
baseline: Public stream memory operations, events and tiny kernels.
confounders: Reduction is on a semaphore word, not array data. Clocks and visibility domains must not be conflated.
gate: K-level until a safe public equivalent is used; no live CUDA-owned pushbuffer patching.

title: Dependent QMD minimal experiment
question: Is there a usable restricted descriptor dependency beyond public graph execution?
setup: First resolve ownership, units, reference counts, cache visibility and completion from implementation evidence. Only then consider two finite known kernels.
sweep: A single dependency/release relation before any circular or dynamic structure.
observe: Correct bounded execution and total cost versus graph replay.
baseline: Public instantiated graphs and batched launches.
confounders: Descriptor fields alone do not prove arbitrary graph semantics or SM affinity. No self-modifying live descriptors.
gate: S/K frontier; no executable low-level command generator supplied.

title: Binary transformation validation
question: Does an edited cubin preserve semantics and improve the intended bottleneck?
setup: Pin compiler/tool/architecture and hash original/edited binaries. Validate metadata, relocations, def/use and dependency controls before differential execution.
sweep: Boundary inputs, resource pressure, memory latency and compiler baseline variants.
observe: Exact or bounded outputs plus isolated and full-kernel performance evidence.
baseline: Original ptxas output and source-level alternatives.
confounders: A transformation can pass warm-cache tests yet fail under variable latency; random tests alone do not establish legality.
gate: B-level edits isolated to controlled experiments, not a claim of universal kernel rewriting.

title: MPS and process interference
question: What sharing, latency and failure boundaries hold on this exact Volta stack?
setup: Use compatible documented MPS/IPC configurations and benign finite workloads in separate clients.
sweep: Client count, resource fractions, work mix and isolated versus shared execution.
observe: Per-client tails, aggregate useful work and observed interference.
baseline: Separate conventional contexts and single-client runs.
confounders: Current MPS docs may include unsupported newer variants; resource shares do not prove fairness or fatal-fault isolation.
gate: No deliberate fault injection on shared hardware; preserve process/resource lifetimes.

title: Launch, graphs and CDP
question: Which supported submission mechanism best matches task granularity?
setup: Compare finite equivalent stages through host launches, instantiated graphs and supported device-side launch variants.
sweep: Task size, repetition, parameter updates and dependency structure.
observe: Host overhead, device idle gaps and total completion time.
baseline: Properly batched launches with minimized unnecessary synchronization.
confounders: Device-side launch is not a remote launch; modern graph/CDP features need exact target/version verification.
gate: Installed compatible APIs and per-device cooperative checks.

title: Power and steady-state behavior
question: Is the proposed schedule faster after thermal and power transients settle?
setup: Run equal-work schedules to stable conditions under unchanged supported limits; record clocks, temperature, power and useful outputs.
sweep: Overlap ratio, phase order, neighbor activity and workload duration.
observe: Sustained throughput and energy per result with raw telemetry context.
baseline: Maximum-overlap and simple fixed schedules.
confounders: Sensor averaging, ambient changes and reduced precision/work can manufacture apparent gains.
gate: No voltage/firmware modifications or unsafe power-limit changes.

title: RAS contamination audit
question: Are performance or correctness observations confounded by hardware errors or recovery?
setup: Read ECC, retired-page, link and management status before/after a normal finite benchmark.
sweep: Normal repeated runs and existing health differences only.
observe: Explicit exclusion/annotation of contaminated samples.
baseline: Clean stable runs on the same device.
confounders: Reset can involve NVLink peers; error absence in one log is not proof of perfect hardware.
gate: Read-only audit; no intentional ECC/link fault injection or routine resets.

title: Platform and electrical evidence
question: Which module/baseboard details affect software-visible behavior?
setup: Collect exact SKU/part/VBIOS/BDF identifiers and available original platform documentation; inspect topology without physical modification.
sweep: Device/OEM revisions, link widths, root placement and supported telemetry.
observe: A source-backed platform matrix with explicit unresolved pins/rails/clock domains.
baseline: Generic V100 assumptions, used only as hypotheses to check.
confounders: SXM2 form factor does not prove identical wiring, firmware or enabled features.
gate: Read-only first; no probing unknown powered pins or firmware modifications.

title: toolchain and library compatibility
question: Which installed artifacts actually execute native sm70 paths?
setup: Compile a tiny native sm70 kernel with the intended toolchain; inspect cubin/fatbin and record driver/library build paths.
sweep: Compiler versions, PTX/cubin selection and required library operators.
observe: A per-feature compatibility matrix rather than a blanket CUDA-version claim.
baseline: A preserved known-working sm70 toolchain and native binary.
confounders: New driver API spelling does not imply a new hardware feature; management displayed version is not compiler version.
gate: No assumption that latest library releases retain Volta support.

title: New PTX spelling on old silicon
question: Does lop3.BoolOp expose useful sm70 code beyond the compiler baseline?
setup: Compile exact documented BoolOp syntax under a compatible PTX/ptxas version and inspect the native instruction and predicate path.
sweep: Truth functions, predicate operation, live outputs and source expressions.
observe: Correct truth tables plus any avoided result-test or predicate instruction.
baseline: Clear CUDA Boolean expressions compiled for sm70.
confounders: PTX 8.2 introduction is not a newer GPU requirement here, but installed compiler parsing still matters.
gate: Exact target notes and operand syntax checked before compilation.

title: Negative-space falsification
question: Which attractive interpretation is actually unsupported or algebraically wrong?
setup: Write the required primitive/contract, then check exact target/form, interface and algebra before any performance experiment.
sweep: Claims such as partial-warp MMA, DMA array reduction, automatic peer coherence or generic semiring MMA.
observe: A minimal contradiction or missing-contract statement attached to the rejected idea.
baseline: A supported equivalent with explicit software work.
confounders: Failure of one interface does not prove silicon impossibility; header presence does not prove usability.
gate: No malformed opcode/command execution merely to see whether it crashes.

title: Complete composition usefulness
question: Does the new representation improve the actual problem after all costs?
setup: Implement equal semantic workloads for a strong conventional, representation-changing and alternate-resource candidate.
sweep: Shape, sparsity, distribution, reuse, accuracy and topology, including held-out cases.
observe: End-to-end time/tails, memory use, energy and validity with a explainable crossover.
baseline: Best applicable existing algorithm, not a straw-man scalar implementation.
confounders: Preprocessing, maintenance, decoding, synchronization and output contracts must be included.
gate: All relevant correctness/capability tests passed; retain negative results.
